data.name: Kifat
data.gender_notes: Kifat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Kifat means 'message', 'news', or 'announcement'. This name is rooted in the rich tradition of Islamic communication, particularly the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) revelation of the Quran. The name Kifat carries the meaning “Message, news” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kifat usually hope their child will grow to embody message, news and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kifat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Message, news.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kifat total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Kifat ibn Abdallah Al-Juhani was a famous Muslim scholar and poet from Yemen. He is known for his comprehensive work Tafsir Al-Kifah which covers the interpretation of the entire Quran. He lived during the 12th and 13th centuries (580-640 AH).

Kifah, a city in ancient Arabia, was a major center for early Islamic learning. It is believed that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab to conquer and establish a garrison in Kifah in 632 AD. Scholars from all over the Islamic world came to study at its renowned universities during the Umayyad and Abbasid periods (661-1258 AD).
